candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin storage and medication teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Teach safe insulin storage: refrigerate unopened insulin at the recommended temperature when possible, never use frozen insulin, protect it from heat/sunlight, and follow product-specific room-temperature limits.

options.A: Keep unopened insulin in a household freezer until first use, then thaw it at room temperature.
options.B: Keep unopened insulin refrigerated at about 36°F to 46°F when possible, never use insulin that has been frozen, and follow the specific product label for room-temperature limits.
options.C: Store unopened insulin at room temperature indefinitely because refrigeration is unnecessary before the first dose.
options.D: Keep insulin near a warm appliance or sunny window so it remains close to body temperature before injection.

candidate.rationale: FDA states that insulin manufacturers recommend refrigeration at approximately 36°F to 46°F; unopened insulin stored this way maintains potency until the labeled expiration date. FDA also states to avoid freezing and not to use insulin that has been frozen, and to keep insulin away from direct heat and sunlight. Room-temperature allowances depend on product and conditions, so the product label should be followed. Therefore B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Unopened insulin should generally be refrigerated at approximately 36°F to 46°F when possible; frozen insulin should not be used, heat/sunlight should be avoided, and room-temperature storage depends on the product and conditions.
